why_retroactive: the generating script was never written to disk; _lead4/ held 8 PNG + 3 JSON + 1 MD and no script. The definition was recovered verbatim from the producing session transcript, so this archive is itself a retroactive migration.

definition.background: exact modal 24-bit RGB per image (np.argmax over unique-value counts, no quantization)
definition.rowCorr: Pearson r of per-row ink counts
definition.colCorr: Pearson r of per-column ink counts
definition.flatBgPct: 100 * max(modal pixel count over the two images) / (H*W)
definition.verdict_rule: UNTESTABLE if flatBgPct > 99.9 (whole canvas is one flat colour -> the ink mask is the empty set by construction, so "low overlap" is vacuously true; evaluated FIRST because with an empty mask the corr and ink metrics carry no information); STRUCT-RELATED if inkOv >= 50 and max(|rowCorr|,|colCorr|) >= 0.5; UNRELATED/FAKE if inkOv < 50 and max(|rowCorr|,|colCorr|) < 0.5; BORDERLINE otherwise
definition.untestable_boundary: Hard condition flatBgPct > 99.9. In this 16-row set it isolates exactly one row (depot, 100.0) with 13.0pp of margin to the next highest (calendar, 87.0). High-but-not-100 rows such as box-detail 76.1, base 76.2, state 70.7, enemy 69.8, box-summary 53.0 are measurable and are NOT UNTESTABLE. Do not widen this condition: "high flat background" is a different finding ("measurable but weakly related"), not "untestable".
definition.untestable_branch_provenance: EXTENSION made in this repository, not part of the 2026-09-30 original, which had only the three-way rule and therefore reported depot as UNRELATED/FAKE. The five metric fields are untouched by the extension; only depot's verdict changes, because the original rule lacked this branch. Provenance: metric fields = verbatim recovery from the producing session; UNTESTABLE branch = ours.

cross_validation.note: the two differing rows (headhunt, operator) are the two scenes whose similarity itself differs between the two commits, i.e. different input renders, not a definition difference.
cross_validation.rows_identical_note: 14/16 refers to the FIVE METRIC FIELDS. Verdict counts on this measurement point are now 4 / 2 / 9 / 1 UNTESTABLE after the UNTESTABLE extension; before the extension depot was counted as UNRELATED/FAKE, giving 4 / 2 / 10.
cross_validation.intentional_divergence: depot only - our UNTESTABLE branch; metrics identical.

scenes.verdict_reason: flatBgPct = 100.0: the whole canvas is a single flat colour, so the ink mask is the empty set by construction; an empty mask intersects nothing and its union equals the other mask, so inkOv is necessarily 0.0. That is a degenerate result of the definition, not a measurement of depot. UNTESTABLE - not UNQUALIFIED, and not FAKE. A reader must not conclude depot fabricated anything from this row.

measurement_point.note: measured at ec440bf; the commit this archive lands on is a later HEAD (5aa2ac3). git diff --stat ec440bf..5aa2ac3 -- src/ggrender/scene_card.go src/ggrender/render.go is empty, so the card render is unchanged and the numbers still hold -- but that is a separate verified claim, not that this file measured HEAD.

reading_notes.depot_inkOv_0.0: NOT A MEASUREMENT, NOT A VERDICT. depot flatBgPct=100.0 means the canvas is a single flat color, so the ink mask is the empty set by construction; an empty mask intersects nothing and its union equals the other mask, so inkOv is necessarily 0.0. The metric has no resolving power on a flat-color canvas. UNTESTABLE != UNQUALIFIED -- this row must not be read as depot faking or depot being structurally unrelated.
reading_notes.lottery_most_dangerous_row: sim 0.98358 is the closest non-passing row to the 0.99 gate, while inkOv=8.2 (second lowest of 16) and max(|rowCorr|,|colCorr|)=0.048 (lowest of 16) -> UNRELATED/FAKE. Highest score proximity, lowest structural relatedness. This row is what must stop the next person from trying to push lottery over the 0.99 gate: the score is carried by flat dark background, and raising similarity further would move a structurally unrelated page over the line without moving it toward the baseline.
reading_notes.cross_validation_boundary: 14 of 16 rows are identical to the last digit across all 5 metric fields. The 2 that differ (headhunt, operator) differ because the INPUT RENDERS differ between the two commits (their similarity differs too: 0.96476->0.79983 and 0.84554->0.69063), NOT because the definitions differ. There are not two definitions in conflict; there are two commits that rendered different images. Definition-level agreement is established independently by the calendar row (86.7 / +0.373 / +1.000 / 87.0) and the state row (71.8 / +0.950 / +0.978 / 70.7).

regeneration.why: The archive directory (.audit/content-mask-overlap-20260930/) accepts text files only. Running or importing mask_overlap.py from inside it creates __pycache__/*.pyc there, and no .gitignore rule covers it (git check-ignore exits 1), so the next person to run a bare "git add ." in that directory would commit binary .pyc into an archive whose acceptance criteria include zero binaries. The archive is written to, never executed in.
regeneration.incident: It happened once: importing mask_overlap.py from the archive directory produced .audit/content-mask-overlap-20260930/__pycache__/mask_overlap.cpython-314.pyc. It was removed with rm -rf and never reached any commit (6f444a1 and 1646f40 contain text files only). This section exists so the command that caused it is not written down in a form that invites repeating it.
regeneration.prerequisite: a temporary detached worktree at the measurement commit, which produced tmp/pixel-compare/<scene>/{old,new}.png; remove it afterwards with git worktree remove --force <path>.
steps: python -B <outside-the-repo>/_regen/mask_overlap.py <outside-the-repo>/<probe-dir> base box box-detail box-summary calendar card depot enemy gacha headhunt help lottery missing operator recruit state
notes: -B disables bytecode writing; use it in addition to running from outside the repo, not instead of it.
The script imports nothing from the repository; it only reads the PNGs the harness already wrote under tmp/pixel-compare/.
mask_overlap.py reads <root>/tmp/pixel-compare/report.json for the similarity column, so the harness must have been run first in that same worktree.
